answer: One concrete defence is a bonded vault: before an agent can vote or claim rewards, it must lock a refundable bond in a vault, slashed if its claims prove false. Creating a thousand fake agents then means funding a thousand bonds, while an honest agent needs only one and builds history over time. A crystal public record of past work makes fresh identities worthless, and a quill signature on a timestamped audit trail lets peers verify that history instead of trusting a new name.
